name: Full-stack Next.js
summary: One Next.js app renders pages on the server and holds the API routes and server actions, with Postgres through Drizzle and Auth.js for sign-in. Few moving parts, good for SEO, fast to ship.

fitsWhen.says: pages must rank in search engines

avoidWhen.says: the heart of it is services or data pipelines

frontend.why: Server rendering, streaming and route handlers in one framework; Nuxt or SvelteKit are the same shape for Vue or Svelte teams.

backend.why: Route handlers and server actions keep the API next to the pages that use it.

database.why: Relational data; a serverless Postgres (Neon) pairs with serverless functions.

auth.why: OAuth and email sign-in with sessions in the database, no extra service.

cache.why: Only when rate limits or a job queue are needed.

ci-cd.why: Checks on every pull request; the platform builds previews.

observability.why: Errors from both the browser and the server functions.

testing.why: End-to-end tests matter most when the server renders the pages.

hosting.why: Preview deployments per branch; a Node server on Fly or a VM also runs Next.js.

services.name: app
responsibilities: Route handlers and server actions for writes

environments.name: dev
environments.hosting: next dev against a local Postgres in Docker

environments.name: staging
environments.purpose: A copy of production for checking a release
environments.hosting: Vercel preview deployments with a Neon branch per pull request

environments.name: prod
environments.hosting: Vercel production with the main Neon branch

notes: No servers to patch; long jobs need a queue elsewhere because functions time out

security.auth: Auth.js database sessions; check the session in every server action and route handler
notes: Validate every input at the API boundary and return typed errors, never stack traces.
Parameterised queries only (the ORM), so no SQL is built from strings.
Set secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies or short-lived tokens; rate-limit sign-in.
Check authorisation on every endpoint on the server, not only in the UI (OWASP A01 Broken Access Control).
Server actions are public endpoints: validate their input with zod.

conventions: Server components by default; 'use client' only where interaction needs it

adrs.title: One app instead of front end plus API
adrs.decision: Pages, API and server actions live in one Next.js app.
adrs.why: Fewer deploys and no CORS; the API has no second client yet.

adrs.title: Serverless Postgres
adrs.why: Scales to zero and gives each preview its own database branch.
